rows.lacks: F2-A10 (f), as clarified (clarifications.md), said that below three quarters of full the forecast falls as the level rises. On the held-out set, run once on the tested commit (3de26e0b, and the same on 81eadac9), it does on 110 of 111 cases below three quarters: adv-h-1’s vocal, at 32, reads 0.828, 0.899 and 0.764 at its level, a third and two thirds of the way to full. The twenty sessions’ growth falls with the level there, as the model gives it (tests/decisions-advice.test.ts, [N], played on tuning seeds). The forecast is in points of result, and what an ability point is worth on the work isn’t monotone in the level everywhere: it is the judge’s curve, and the forecast reads it truly (adv-h-1 forecast 0.828 and brought 1.058; F2-A10 (e) holds). Preparation apart from training holds on 120 of 120, and near mastery the ladder falls on 30 of 30. Should (f)’s diminishing returns be read in the growth the twenty sessions bring, with the forecast’s points left to the judge’s curve; or does (f) stay not met as clarified?

F2-A10 (h), as clarified (clarifications.md), said the trained input’s forecast at the discipline it had when it was advised falls after the twenty sessions, on every case. On the held-out set, run once on the tested commit (3de26e0b, and the same on 81eadac9), it does on 116 of 120. In the four that didn’t (adv-h-1 vocal at 32, adv-h-22 emotional depth at 27, adv-h-102 memory at 91, adv-h-111 focus at 93), the forecast itself fell, so (h) as written holds there; the input’s own part rose because what an ability point is worth on the work isn’t monotone in the level (the judge’s curve, as in (f)). As written, the forecast fell on 113 of 120; the 7 that rose (adv-h-91, 100, 103, 106, 107, 110, 118, all near mastery) rose by a thousandth or less, each within discipline’s lift and said. Every case fell, or rose within discipline’s lift and said: 120 of 120. The first-named changed wherever another led, 51 of 51. Should (h) read: after the twenty sessions the forecast falls, or a rise is no more than discipline’s lift and is said; or does (h) stay not met, as written and as clarified?

Measured, it isn’t (2 of 44), and the sorting brief 11 asked for says why: nothing in the game is missing, and the clause, with (c), (e) and (g)’s second and third items, asks what the approved design rules out at this budget. Which comparison and which floor should hold the owner’s “meaningful opportunities to make a valid restrained interpretation work, even where a scene favors larger expression”, given one strength that mustn’t erase unrelated weaknesses, fair budgets, no restraint bonus and no rebalancing of the judge?

The term of a non-verified (Not For Federal Identification) Connecticut card issued to somebody not a citizen, such as an F-1 student: no page or law the state publishes gives one. The non-driver ID page says 'valid for 7 years' with no exception; the limited-term REAL ID, whose expiration 'must align with the expiration date on the individual's legal status document(s)' (one year where there's none), is for DACA holders only ('Currently, only residents with Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) status are eligible'); Regs. Conn. State Agencies § 14-137-64a(c) lets the commissioner revoke the card once its holder is 'no longer entitled to be present', and sets no term; CGS chapter 246 has no such provision (searched for 'authorized stay', 'lawful status', 'immigration status', 'visa', 'legal presence', 'citizen'). SLATE keeps the term to the end of lawful presence as its assumption, said so in systems/identity.ts and on the guide's line ('SLATE's reading where the state publishes none'). Also not said by the DMV, and taken by SLATE: whether a non-citizen the DMV doesn't ask back has the twenty days from the first visit (SLATE takes the later, its described return after SAVE); and whose holidays the twenty business days skip (SLATE counts the federal ones). What would settle it: the DMV's answer in writing (its Contact Center, 860-263-5700, or a published policy). Pages tried and not reached: https://digital.ct.gov/dmv/licenses/licenses/non-driver-id-card/non-driver-photo-id---obtaining (2026-10-16: host doesn't resolve, WebFetch ENOTFOUND, the proxy's CONNECT 502); https://eregulations.ct.gov/eRegsPortal/Browse/RCSA/Title_01Subtitle_01-1hSection_01-1h-1/ to -8 and Title_01Subtitle_01-1h/ (2026-10-16: 'Unable to Access Resource (HTTP: 404)'; read instead in the DMV's 2007 compilation, https://portal.ct.gov/-/media/DMV/20/29/mvregspdf.pdf). www.cga.ct.gov was reached only after completing its certificate chain with GoDaddy's G2 intermediate from certs.godaddy.com, the server sending its leaf alone (curl error 60 otherwise; WebFetch 503).
